sources.entry: LayerX - Intuitive app to display transparent images on screen.

summary.one_liner: LayerX is a macOS app for displaying transparent images as floating, always-on-top windows on screen.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you drag and drop or paste (⌘V) an image or file onto the screen. You can scale it to actual size, up or down by 10%, or by 1px, with aspect ratio scaling. Arrow keys nudge the image 1px at a time. Transparency can be adjusted with ⌘J and ⌘K or by scrolling over the image. Images can be locked, the window can be kept always on top (⌘T) or on all spaces (⌘A), and ⌘L locks images and pins the window on top.
use_cases: overlay an image on top of other windows
compare a design mockup against a live app
trace or align artwork on screen
keep a reference image visible while working
adjust transparency of a picture on the desktop
notable: Drag-and-drop or clipboard paste to load images
Keyboard-driven scaling, nudging, and transparency control
Lock images so they stay in place
Can stay on top of and across all macOS spaces
caveats: Requires Mac OS X 10.10 or later
README gives no installation instructions or download link
README does not state a version or maintenance status
